title: AOS Space Data Link Protocol
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: The Document Control table (PDF p. 7) marks 732.0-B-4 (October 2021) as the current issue and B-1 (September 2003), B-2 (July 2006) and B-3 (September 2015) as superseded. Issue 4 adds clarifications and support for the SDLS Extended Procedures (CCSDS 355.1-B-1), a new normative PICS Annex A, and a new informative Annex D on OID frame randomization.
summary:
The CCSDS Recommended Standard for the **Advanced Orbiting Systems (AOS) Space Data Link Protocol**. AOS is a Data Link Layer protocol with fixed-length frames that carries packets, bitstreams and other data over space-to-ground, ground-to-space and space-to-space links, mostly for high-rate return links. It sits beside the [TM](../ccsds/tm-sdlp.md) and [TC](../ccsds/tc-sdlp.md) protocols and below the [Space Packet](../ccsds/space-packet.md) and [Encapsulation](../ccsds/encapsulation.md) protocols. Frame length and synchronisation come from the [TM Synchronization and Channel Coding](../ccsds/tm-coding.md) sublayer (or FACM or DVB-S2). The wiki page is [AOS](../ccsds/aos.md).

Section 2 gives an overview of the protocol: Physical, Master and Virtual Channels, the services and the functions. Section 3 defines the seven services: Virtual Channel Packet (VCP), Bitstream, Virtual Channel Access (VCA), VC Operational Control Field (VC_OCF), Virtual Channel Frame (VCF), Master Channel Frame (MCF) and Insert. Section 4 specifies the AOS Version 2 Transfer Frame. Its 6- or 8-octet Primary Header carries a 2-bit Version '01', an 8-bit SCID, a 6-bit VCID, a 24-bit VC Frame Count, a Signaling Field (Replay Flag, VC Frame Count Cycle) and an optional RS(10,6) Frame Header Error Control. The frame also has an optional Insert Zone, a Data Field holding an M_PDU (11-bit First Header Pointer), a B_PDU (14-bit Bitstream Data Pointer) or a VCA_SDU, an optional 4-octet OCF and an optional 2-octet FECF. Section 4 then gives the sending and receiving procedures (multiplexing, idle data, OID frames on VCID 63). Section 5 tabulates the managed parameters, and section 6 restates the frame, procedures and parameters with the [SDLS](../ccsds/sdls.md) Security Header and Trailer.

key_points.text: The protocol provides seven services: Virtual Channel Packet, Bitstream, Virtual Channel Access, VC_OCF, Virtual Channel Frame, Master Channel Frame and Insert.

Issue 4 (October 2021) is current. It adds support for the SDLS Extended Procedures, a PICS proforma (Annex A) and OID frame randomization examples (Annex D). Issues B-1 (2003), B-2 (2006) and B-3 (2015) are superseded.

An AOS Transfer Frame consists of a Primary Header (6 or 8 octets), an optional Insert Zone, the Data Field, an optional 4-octet Operational Control Field and an optional 2-octet Frame Error Control Field. Its length is constant for a mission phase on a Physical Channel.

The Primary Header holds the Master Channel ID (2-bit Transfer Frame Version Number plus 8-bit Spacecraft ID), a 6-bit VCID, a 24-bit VC Frame Count, an 8-bit Signaling Field and an optional 2-octet Frame Header Error Control.
The Transfer Frame Version Number is '01', which denotes the AOS Version 2 Transfer Frame. SANA assigns the 8-bit Spacecraft ID according to CCSDS 320.0-M.
VCID 'all ones' (63) is reserved for Only Idle Data (OID) Transfer Frames. The valid user VCIDs are 0-62 and need not be consecutive.
The VC Frame Count is a 24-bit sequential count, modulo 16,777,216, of frames on each Virtual Channel. It must not be reset early unless that is unavoidable.
In the Signaling Field, the Replay Flag (bit 40) is 0 for realtime and 1 for replay frames. The VC Frame Count Cycle Use Flag and the 4-bit VC Frame Count Cycle extend the frame count.

The optional Frame Header Error Control (bits 48-63) is a shortened Reed-Solomon (10,6) code with 4-bit symbols and E=2 symbol-correction capability that can protect the 10-bit MCID, the 6-bit VCID and the 8-bit Signaling Field.
M_PDU header: bits 0-4 are a reserved spare and bits 5-15 are the First Header Pointer. 'All ones' means no packet starts in the frame, and 'all ones minus one' means idle data only.
B_PDU header: bits 0-1 are a reserved spare and bits 2-15 are the Bitstream Data Pointer. 'All ones' means the frame is full of valid data, and 'all ones minus one' means idle data only.

Managed parameters of a Physical Channel include the Transfer Frame Length, Version Number 2, the valid SCIDs, the MC multiplexing scheme, and the presence of FHEC, Insert Zone (with its length) and FECF.
The Data Field Content of each Virtual Channel is managed as one of M_PDU, B_PDU, VCA_SDU or Idle Data. The presence of the VC_OCF is also managed per Virtual Channel.
With SDLS, a managed parameter per Virtual Channel indicates the presence of the Security Header. The Security Header and Trailer surround the Data Field and shorten it.
The OID randomizer LFSR (Fibonacci or Galois form) is initialised only at device start-up, not per frame, and generates the pattern FF FF FF FF 6D B6 D8 61 45 1F ...

notes: PDF pages 1-2 are duplicate covers. The extracted text has 113 form-feed pages (registry: 112); the last one is empty. The frame and header figures come out as scattered labels in the text, but the field definitions are in the clauses. 1.5 says the document has 'six numbered sections and three annexes', although it has four annexes (A-D); Annex D is new in issue 4. The normative SDLS reference [10] is still issue 1 (355.0-B-1, 2015), but the library also holds 355.0-B-2 (slug ccsds-355-0-355x0b2). Reference [11] is dated February 2020 here, while CCSDS 355.0-B-2 dates the same document February 2019. No individual authors are named. The registry copy was taken from ccsds.org on 2026-11-12.
